entry_points.text: Fault picks page by offset: zero is run struct, PIO is arch data, coalesced is machine ring when enabled, dirty-window is ring pages, else arch fault with refcount. Mmap rejects exec or non-shared mappings touching the ring window, else installs fault ops.

Per-vCPU debug makes an id-named dir with read-only pid file plus arch hook. Stats use a read-only id-named file via generic helper with cloexec reservation; release drops VM ref. Pre-fault needs clear flags and aligned range, holds loaded state and srcu, aborts on signal or bad status, succeeding if any page progressed.

Control rejects foreign space, dead VM, non-virt types, waits for online, offers arch unlocked handling first, then takes vCPU mutex and dispatches run, regs, MP, debug, sigmask, FPU, stats, pre-fault, else arch. Compat intercepts only sigmask. Early calls without online wait risk null array use.

Device ops delegate mmap, attr, and control; attr needs accessor, unknown controls use custom hook else invalid. Create bounds-checks type, honors test-only, creates under VM lock with publish, inits outside, takes ref and fd, unwinding on failure. Weak defaults reject caps, decline compat, empty shutdown.

VM ioctl checks owner and liveness then routes create, caps, memory, dirty, events, IRQs, routing, attrs, device, extensions, ring, stats, guest mem, else arch. Compat tries arch-compat first and translates dirty requests. VM fops expose release, ioctls, seek. Stats, create, version, sizing, top extensions follow reserve, wrap, install, unwind discipline.

exports.text: GFNs resolve via owning slot to host address, page, or pinned vCPU mapping with writability out. Map clears pointers, stores frame and flags, then direct-maps or I/O-remaps. Dirty resolves slot first; descriptor holds pages, pointer, frame, flags, host frame.
Kick tries light wake; self flips in-guest to exiting-guest without IPI or atomics, else after arch check signals another online in-range CPU; migration may stale target safely as it forces exit.

hazards.text: Extension switch is truncated; full set and unknown fallback must not be assumed. ABI reports mem, dirty, event, cap, halt-poll, MSI, coalesced support with stable version, ids, mapping length. Foreign or dead calls fail I/O error. Routing needs arch permission, max count, clear flags. Mapping reuse warns once and releases first. Bad guest address, SPAPR issues, read-only clears warn or reject early.

invariants.text: Dirty ring is a window from ring size. Ring-bitmap needs bitmap build, existing size, no flags, empty slots under slot mutex. Halt-poll is width-limited then published. Extensions report levels or neutral. Device types index a bounded table, null as missing.
vCPU fds are id-named anonymous inodes with vCPU data, RW cloexec. Sigmask strips kill/stop, null clears, with native and compat length checks. Fixed get/set copy via temp buffers to arch helpers.

Mem versions share a build-checked prefix; legacy is zero-extended and flag-masked. Virt-enable defaults on then read-only; per-CPU state under usage mutex and count. Hinted bus write checks overlap else full search; order uses shared comparator, free is RCU-deferred.

Stats use one offset in VM or per-vCPU counters, summed on read, zeroed per vCPU on clear, zero-only; global walks hold the VM-list mutex. Debug open takes a VM ref with decimal simple-attr transfers. Perf is inactive outside PMI guest, else active plus user; PT hooks empty. An accessor exposes current vCPU.

VFIO helpers resolve dynamically; absent is no-op, false, or null. Add validates VFIO, rejects dups, links with ref; remove detaches or misses; coherency rescans and only on change touches DMA; SPAPR attach caches group under device mutex then attaches. Only file-group add, remove, SPAPR ops allowed. Second device is busy; release drains entries and frees state. Creation needs VM lock.

locks.text: Online wait checks count then killably takes vCPU mutex, interrupted on signal, I/O error if unreachable. Bus lookup needs VM srcu read, missing bus or range yields null.
Device release holds VM lock while RCU-removing, syncing, then invoking release; ref drops always. File-to-device succeeds only when file ops match device ops.

Bypass register and unregister serialize tables under one mutex. Producer keys by event identity, records IRQ, inserts, connects on same-key consumer with rollback on failure; unregister disconnects, erases, clears; empty is no-op, double bind invalid. Mismatched erasure warns.

state_machines.text: Creation validates id and max, rejects overflow and dups, arch pre-checks, allocates vCPU and run page, inits, arch-creates, optionally allocs ring, inserts, creates fd, publishes online with debug. Failure unwinds index, ring, arch, pages, count, array, refs. VM lock covers validation and insert, then vCPU mutex covers fd and online increment with barrier.

Run needs zero arg, refreshes thread id via arch notify, sets wants-run, arch-runs, clears flag, exits and traces. Sched-in clears preempted and ready, publishes occupant, arch-loads; sched-out sets scheduled-out, conditionally preempted and ready, arch-puts, clears occupant. Notifier-to-vCPU is container lookup. Pid reads take read lock, updates under write lock.

Ring sizing runs once before any vCPU, needs offset cap and power-of-two length covering reserved entries plus a page within max, under VM mutex. Reset walks vCPUs under slot mutex with TLB flush on progress; empty check needs slot mutex. Enable is idempotent; online aborts on failure, offline disables, shutdown disables all, suspend and resume assert lock and IRQ state.

structs.text: Follow params bundle slot, frame, address, flags, pin request, writable out, and page out only for refcounted or pinned pages. vCPU file ops expose release, controls, mmap, no-op seek; VM ops only fault; release drops the machine ref.

VM stats file is read-only anonymous via shared formatter, release drops VM ref, seek no-op, private data is the VM. Compat dirty and clear carry narrowed bitmap in a width-preserving union, translated by widening pointer and copying scalars.
Control device is a misc device under the virt name with ioctl, no-op seek, and shared compat handling. Two header guards protect the MM-internal and VFIO headers.
